chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala ibn Ayyub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:

I said to him, 'A man circumambulated the House and became certain that he had performed eight shawt (circuits).' He said, 'He adds six to them. And likewise, if he becomes certain that he has performed eight circuits between al-Safa and al-Marwah, let him add six to them.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Safa and Al-Marwah (the two hills between which Sa'i is performed)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they are certain they completed the required number of Tawaf or Sa'i circuits?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who is certain of having completed the minimum required circuits but seeks to ensure validity by adding extra rounds. Specifically, if one is certain of eight circuits, they should add six more, bringing the total to fourteen, a practice rooted in the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and precaution (*ihtiyat*) in Shia jurisprudence. This highlights the scholarly distinction between absolute certainty (*yaqin*) and the need for additional verification in ritual purity and worship.
